claims.text: refund-requirements.md@stage-2 lines 41-50 hold a second list, 'Yêu cầu phi chức năng', after the functional YC-1..YC-6: YC-7 to YC-10.
YC-7: the customer's refund request is received and answered within 2 seconds, even when the payment gateway does not answer or reports an error.
YC-8: each refund request keeps who asked and when; neither can be changed or deleted later, so accounting can reconcile.

YC-9: an order is never refunded twice, even when sending to the gateway must be retried. YC-10: when the gateway fails, the request is resent automatically for at least 24 hours before going to staff.

YC-1..YC-6 describe what happens (own paid order, full amount, no second request, confirmed refund cancels the order and emails, refused refund to staff) and say nothing about the gateway being down or records being editable.
A design that calls the gateway inside the customer's request and waits for its answer cannot answer within 2 seconds when the gateway does not answer, so YC-7 rules it out.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-2: docs/design/refund-design.md:39-43 (rejected option, ruled out by YC-7)

claims.text: At stage-1 PlaceOrderAsync calls notifier.Send inside the request, so the order response waits for whatever Send does; backend.l2.work-outside-the-request shows that once Send talks to a mail server, the response waits on (and can fail because of) it.
A non-functional requirement is useful only when it names a case and a measure; it can rule out designs, so it is written with the functional ones, not after the features work.
